macro_actions.name: Psychoeducation and Normalization
macro_actions.description: Therapist explains the nature of panic and anxiety symptoms, normalizes these experiences, and differentiates adaptive from maladaptive anxiety.

goal.objective: Increase the patient’s understanding of anxiety/panic and reduce fear, shame, or catastrophizing.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately understands anxiety/panic as manageable and non-dangerous, reducing distress surrounding symptoms.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient grasps the basics of anxiety/panic and feels somewhat less threatened, but retains mild fears or misconceptions.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains fearful and holds mistaken catastrophic beliefs about anxiety/panic symptoms.

goal.reward_hint: Patient appropriately describes panic/anxiety with reduced catastrophizing or increased acceptance.

states: Patient exhibits fear or confusion about anxiety/panic.
Patient expresses catastrophic beliefs or shame regarding symptoms.
Therapy is beginning or moving to intervention rationale.

macro_actions.name: Objective Self-Monitoring and Recordkeeping
macro_actions.description: Therapist trains and motivates the patient to systematically record panic attacks, anxiety events, mood states, and coping efforts using standardized forms.

goal.objective: Increase patient self-awareness and provide a data-driven foundation for all subsequent interventions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently and objectively records relevant events, leading to accurate insights and treatment planning.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient completes most records but may be subjective or occasionally skip entries.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Records are consistently missing, incomplete, or inaccurate, hindering progress.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist receives consistently completed, objective monitoring records from the patient.

states: Patient is unfamiliar with monitoring tools or unsure about own symptoms/events.
Therapist introduces or reinforces foundational treatment strategies.
Patient exhibits reluctance or concern about recordkeeping.

macro_actions.name: Guided Analysis and Insight Building
macro_actions.description: Therapist reviews monitoring records with patient, collaboratively identifying patterns, triggers, and cycles of panic/anxiety.

goal.objective: Foster understanding of personal anxiety cycles, triggers, and maintenance factors.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates insight into own patterns and can identify specific triggers and cycles.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient recognizes some patterns or triggers with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient fails to recognize key patterns or triggers despite guidance.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes awareness or makes connections between triggers and panic/anxiety episodes.

states: Patient has accumulated monitoring records but lacks clarity regarding their meaning.
Therapist aims to move from data gathering to insight development.
Patient is uncertain about what drives their panic/anxiety episodes.

macro_actions.name: Collaborative Cognitive Restructuring
macro_actions.description: Therapist educates and guides the patient to identify, analyze, and challenge maladaptive thoughts and beliefs related to anxiety and panic.

goal.objective: Modify unrealistic, catastrophic, or unhelpful thoughts to reduce anxiety and panic intensity.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately applies cognitive restructuring strategies independently and beliefs shift towards realistic interpretations.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient uses cognitive restructuring with therapist help and beliefs show partial improvement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient continues to hold maladaptive beliefs, unable to challenge or change thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient evidences change or flexibility in previously held catastrophic thoughts.

states: Patient expresses automatic negative or catastrophic thoughts about panic/anxiety.
Therapist introduces cognitive strategies following psychoeducation.
Patient struggles to separate facts from assumptions.

macro_actions.name: Systematic Skills Training and Behavioral Practice
macro_actions.description: Therapist teaches coping skills (e.g., breathing, relaxation, exposure) and guides application through repeated in-session and homework practice.

goal.objective: Build patient self-efficacy with coping skills for managing anxiety and panic.

success_levels.ideal: Patient independently uses coping skills during anxiety, resulting in decreased symptom intensity and avoidance.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient practices skills but is inconsistent or requires therapist reminders. Occasional improvement in coping.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids practice or fails to use skills effectively, resulting in little or no symptom improvement.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates coping skills in session or reports consistent practice outside session.

states: Patient is anxious or anticipates panic but lacks adequate coping responses.
Therapist moves from discussion to skill-building stages.
Patient is ready for practical behavioral intervention.

macro_actions.name: Graded Exposure Planning and Execution
macro_actions.description: Therapist collaborates with patient to design exposure hierarchies and guides gradual, systematic practice facing feared situations or physical sensations.

goal.objective: Reduce avoidance and anxiety/fear response to targeted triggers through direct experience.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently completes planned exposures, demonstrates reduced avoidance and fear, and alters maladaptive beliefs.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts exposures with some anxiety but partial reduction in avoidance/fear.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids exposure tasks; maintains high anxiety and avoidance behavior.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reports successful approach behaviors toward previously avoided situations or sensations.

states: Patient identifies specific avoided situations/physical symptoms.
Therapist introduces exposure interventions.
Patient demonstrates willingness to face or attempt exposure but needs guidance.

macro_actions.name: Review, Consolidation, and Troubleshooting
macro_actions.description: Therapist reviews skill use and exposure outcomes with patient for consolidation, insight building, problem solving, and adjustment of strategies.

goal.objective: Consolidate learning, reinforce progress, and troubleshoot obstacles to improve future outcomes.

success_levels.ideal: Patient articulates learning, applies insights to setbacks, and shows resilience/adaptation.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient identifies some gains or obstacles, makes moderate adjustments for next steps.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient does not consolidate learning, repeats maladaptive patterns, fails to adapt strategy.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reflects on exposure/skill outcomes and proposes adjustments or acknowledges new understanding.

states: Patient completes exposure or skill application but struggles to generalize or understand results.
Therapist moves from practice to integration phase.
Follow-up session after behavioral interventions.

macro_actions.name: Involvement of Significant Others and Team-Based Support
macro_actions.description: Therapist evaluates, coaches, and prepares significant others to provide appropriate support during exposure and coping, facilitating teamwork while minimizing rescue and reinforcement of avoidance.

goal.objective: Enhance patient progress via coordinated involvement of helpers, while increasing patient independence.

success_levels.ideal: Helpers support exposure efforts appropriately and patient transitions to independent coping.
success_levels.acceptable: Helpers are somewhat supportive; patient relies on assistance but begins practicing increased independence.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Helpers reinforce avoidance or are absent, patient remains dependent or sabotages progress.

goal.reward_hint: Patient and helpers collaborate constructively and patient progressively self-manages exposure.

states: Patient's support network can influence avoidance or progress.
Therapist discusses barriers/enablers related to significant others.
Patient demonstrates readiness or need for collaborative exposure.

macro_actions.name: Medication Management and Transition Support
macro_actions.description: Therapist educates patient about medication use for panic/anxiety, coordinates with medical providers, and supports safe withdrawal and skill substitution.

goal.objective: Patient safely discontinues unneeded medications while maintaining progress with CBT coping skills.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes withdrawal, manages symptoms using CBT with minimal relapse.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient tapers medication, experiences mild withdrawal managed with support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient relapses or is unable to discontinue medication, coping skills are insufficient.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates safe medication reduction and relies increasingly on CBT strategies.

states: Patient is prescribed medication for panic/anxiety.
Therapist discusses treatment planning related to pharmacological support.
Patient or prescriber initiates medication tapering.

macro_actions.name: Maintenance Planning and Relapse Prevention
macro_actions.description: Therapist guides patient in developing ongoing practice plans, prepares for setbacks, problem-solves anticipated stressors, and supports long-term personal goal setting.

goal.objective: Ensure patient maintains gains, is resilient to setbacks, and self-monitors for continued progress post-therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient establishes and follows a maintenance plan, confidently manages future stressors with CBT skills.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient engages in some maintenance activities and copes with minor setbacks; may need booster sessions.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient has no structured plan, relapses easily when stressed, and abandons learned skills.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates personal goals, maintenance routines, and expresses readiness for self-directed progress.

states: Therapy is nearing completion or patient has achieved significant progress.
Patient expresses concern about relapse or future stressors.
Therapist wants to consolidate long-term outcomes and self-efficacy.
